statements.subject: client
statements.description: It MAY be included in GET_PARAMETER requests from the client to the server with only a Range format and no value to request the current media position, whether the session is in Play or Ready state in the included format.
actions: include Range header with format specifier and no value in GET_PARAMETER request

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The server SHALL, if supporting the range format, respond with the current playing point or pause point as the start of the range.
actions: set response Range start to current playing point or pause point

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an explicit stop point was used in the previous PLAY request, then that value shall be included as stop point.
actions: include explicit stop point from previous PLAY request in GET_PARAMETER response Range header

statements.subject: rtsp
statements.description: While octet ranges (Byte Ranges) (see Section 2.1 of [RFC7233]) and other extended units MAY be used, their behavior is unspecified since they are not normally meaningful in RTSP.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Servers supporting the Range header MUST understand the NPT range format and SHOULD understand the SMPTE range format.

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If the Range header is sent in a time format that is not understood, the recipient SHOULD return 456 (Header Field Not Valid for Resource) and include an Accept-Ranges header indicating the supported time formats for the given resource.
actions: return 456 (Header Field Not Valid for Resource)
include Accept-Ranges header listing supported time formats for the resource
